description: Take Charles Bridge apart piece by piece in 3D, and read the story of Prague's medieval river crossing: from Charles IV's foundation stone to the Baroque statues, the floods, and the films.

hotspots.text: The Old Town Bridge Tower is considered one of the most beautiful Gothic gateways in Europe. Bohemian kings passed beneath it on their coronation route to St. Vitus Cathedral. The sculptural decoration was damaged in the Swedish assault of 1648 and never fully restored.
hotspots.title: The Old Town Bridge Tower

hotspots.text: St. John of Nepomuk, the Czech martyr saint thrown from this bridge in 1393, is the most touched statue in Prague: visitors rub the plaque for good luck. Like all 30 statues, what you see is a replica; the originals stand in the Lapidarium.
hotspots.title: St. John of Nepomuk

hotspots.text: One of sixteen sandstone arches. The bridge was built as a bow bridge on the model of the Stone Bridge in Regensburg, and its piers have survived floods, ice floes and two world wars.
hotspots.title: Sixteen arches

hotspots.text: The triangular cutwaters shielding each pier from Vltava ice floes. The Judith Bridge that stood here before was destroyed by a flood in 1342; Charles IV's bridge was engineered not to share its fate.
hotspots.title: Ice guards

hotspots.text: The parapets carry the continuous alley of 30 statues, fifteen per side, erected between 1683 and 1714. They are almost entirely Baroque saints and patron saints of the Czech lands.
hotspots.title: The statue alley

intro: Prague's oldest bridge is 516 meters of sandstone that has carried kings, saints, armies and twenty million tourists. This is how a medieval river crossing became the most filmed bridge in Central Europe.
page_title: Charles Bridge: Exploded 3D Model and History | Architectural Atlas

sections.body:
On 9 July 1357, at 5:31 in the morning, King Charles IV laid the foundation stone of a new bridge over the Vltava. Royal astrologers had chosen the moment for its auspicious alignment of numbers: 1357, the 9th day of the 7th month, at 5:31. The old Judith Bridge had been torn apart by a flood in 1342, and Prague, the imperial capital, needed a crossing worthy of its status.

The king's master builder Peter Parler, already at work on St. Vitus Cathedral, raised a bow bridge of sixteen sandstone arches on massive piers, each shielded by a cutwater ice guard. It was the largest Gothic civil work of its age. When it was completed in the early 1400s, it was simply the Stone Bridge, or the Prague Bridge: for centuries it was the only way across the river, and it made Prague the hinge of the trade route between Eastern and Western Europe.
sections.heading: The king's bridge

sections.body:
The bridge was never just infrastructure. It stood on the coronation route of the Bohemian kings, who processed across it beneath the Old Town Bridge Tower, conceived as a symbolic victory arch. In 1648, in the last battle of the Thirty Years' War, the citizens of the Old Town held the bridge against a Swedish army that had already taken the castle and the Lesser Town; the tower still carries the scars of Swedish cannon fire.

The thirty statues came later, between 1683 and 1714, turning the roadway into an open-air Baroque gallery. St. John of Nepomuk, the priest martyred by being thrown from the bridge in 1393, became the most famous of them. Pilgrims and then tourists have been rubbing his plaque for luck ever since.
sections.heading: Coronations, war and saints

sections.body:
In 1870 the Stone Bridge was renamed for the king who ordered it: Charles Bridge. By then it was no longer the only crossing, but it had become something rarer, a medieval street that still worked. The statues, blackened by coal smoke, were gradually replaced by replicas from 1965 onward; the originals are preserved in the Lapidarium of the National Museum.

Today the bridge is a pedestrian zone and one of the most visited places in Europe. A twenty-year program of structural inspections and repairs began in 2019, because seven centuries of floods, ice and footsteps are a maintenance schedule all of their own.
sections.heading: The most walked bridge in Europe

sections.body:
Brian De Palma opened Mission: Impossible (1996) in Prague, and the first set piece sends Jim Phelps, played by Jon Voight, running across Charles Bridge toward the embassy. The film's Prague is a collage, the embassy is really the Liechtenstein Palace, but the bridge is the real thing, and the shot made it shorthand for the city in Hollywood's imagination.

Spider-Man: Far From Home (2019) used the bridge for one of its quietest scenes: Peter Parker and MJ walk its length while she tells him she has worked out his secret. The statue of Charles IV watches from Krizovnicke Square in the background. The production had the walkway to itself, a luxury no tourist ever gets.

The bridge keeps collecting credits. Vin Diesel passes beneath it in xXx (2002), and Van Helsing (2004) enters the city by boat under its arches, both filmed in Prague. The myth to retire is the idea that the bridge you see in old films is untouched medieval stone: since 1965 every statue on it has been a replica, and the bridge is a careful, ongoing reconstruction of itself.
sections.heading: In the cultural conversation

timeline.text: A flood destroys the Judith Bridge (1158-1172), Prague's first stone bridge.
Charles IV lays the foundation stone at 5:31 am, a moment chosen by royal astrologers.
Construction completes under master builder Peter Parler; the bridge is called the Stone Bridge.
John of Nepomuk is thrown from the bridge on Wenceslas IV's orders; later canonized.
Old Town defenders hold the bridge against the Swedish army in the last battle of the Thirty Years' War.
Thirty Baroque statues are erected along the parapets.
A new bridge opens; Charles Bridge is no longer the only Vltava crossing.
The Stone Bridge is renamed Charles Bridge after its founder.
Statue originals are replaced by replicas; the originals go to the Lapidarium.
Mission: Impossible opens with a chase across the bridge.
Spider-Man: Far From Home films the Peter-and-MJ walk on the bridge; a twenty-year restoration program begins.
